title: After land the orchestrator's checkout is level with origin/main before its next claim
goal: After backlog.py land pushes an item, the orchestrator's next claim starts from the pushed origin/main, either because land fast-forwards the checkout it ran in (clean, on a branch whose upstream is origin/main) or because kb-sprint run step 2 says to fast-forward before a claim, as the gate 'how' decides; kb/_self/backlog.md says which. From the SP-pbekfhaz retrospective: after two landings the orchestrator's checkout was 7 commits behind origin/main and each claim needed a manual git merge --ff-only.

run: import pathlib,sys;t=pathlib.Path("_tools/bl_land.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8");ok="--ff-only" in t;print("land fast-forwards its checkout:",ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: How does the orchestrator's checkout get level with origin/main after a landing?
options: tool: land fast-forwards the checkout it ran in when it is clean and its upstream is origin/main, and says so
rule text: kb-sprint run step 2 says to run git merge --ff-only origin/main before each claim; no tool change
gates.recommendation: tool: land fast-forwards the checkout it ran in when it is clean and its upstream is origin/main, and says so
gates.answer: tool: land fast-forwards the checkout it ran in when it is clean and its upstream is origin/main, and says so

notes: The second check, tests.py -k land, passes before the work on purpose: it pins the landing behaviour the change must keep. The first check fails until land fast-forwards its checkout (operator's gate how: tool).
